title: Cohort upgrade sequencing and support grid for multi-surface LTS
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define and implement a cohort-based upgrade sequencing strategy plus a support matrix that maps LTS runtime versions to compatible API, SDK and Console releases. This ticket covers the sequencing rules, preflight validators, rollout gates, telemetry checks, and the public-facing upgrade guidance for customers and internal SRE/Support.
goals: Create a deterministic cohort schedule (canary -> regional -> cohort waves) that minimizes cross-service incompatibility risk
Publish a support grid that states compatibility guarantees for runtime, API, SDKs, and Console across LTS lanes
Ship automated preflight checks and rollout gates integrated with the deployment pipeline
Ensure rollback paths and emergency mitigation runbooks are validated before wide rollout
proposed_solution: Adopt cohort tiers: canary (internal), 5% customer cohort, regional wave, enterprise cohort, global rollout
Introduce a support grid CSV published with each LTS release listing minimum compatible API version, SDK shims, console feature flags and known incompatibilities
Enforce preflight validators: schema parity tests, backward-compat API smoke, KV cache warmup success rate, end-to-end token latency regression check
Add rollout gate steps in CI/CD: metrics smoke (p99 latency, error rate), consumer API test suite, customer subset opt-out toggle
Provide clear upgrade commands and knob settings for Dedicated and Private deployments, including DB migration stubs and KMS key rotation notes
acceptance_criteria: Published support grid artifact (public and internal) with matrix for runtime-1.20 against API v3 and SDKs (python/js/golang)
Automated preflight suite integrated into deployment pipeline and green on a canary cluster
Rollout automation supports cohort scheduling and can pause/abort based on configured metric thresholds
Runbook validated via tabletop drill with SRE, Support and Customer Success and post-drill notes recorded
implementation_notes: Schema compatibility check will reuse existing runtime/compatibility library (see ENG-12801 for utilities)
Preflight validators implemented as Kubernetes Jobs that emit a standardized 'preflight:pass' metric
Console compatibility warnings surfaced via a feature flag gate and console-2025.03 release notes
Dedicated/private upgrade commands documented under Confluence page and included in on-prem package scripts

rollback_plan: Automatic cohort pause and rollback to previous runtime image on threshold breach
If API surface incompatibility detected, fall back to stable API proxy that rewrites incompatible requests
Manual escalation path to emergency rollback with DBA and infra (runbook link in files)
tests: End-to-end customer flow smoke (chat, embeddings, streaming)
Performance benchmark (per-token latency) and KV cache hit-rate validation
Canary-specific synthetic load with ramping script
migration_steps: Publish support grid and migration notes
Run preflight validators on customer mirrors where available
Schedule customer cohorts and communicate maintenance windows
Monitor telemetry for 48h after each wave before progressing
notes: Avoid coupling cohort progression to single metric; use weighted decision function (latency, errors, quality regression)
Consider a lightweight compatibility shim approach for Console features to reduce forced console rollouts
Follow-up: explore automated SDK minor-version pinning in rollouts to simplify customer experience
